title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
summary: Given a graph $G$, does it have quantum symmetries, or in other words, is the algebra of the quantum automorphism group non-commutative? In the world of ordinary groups, determining whether a finitely presented group is commutative is undecidable. This is an immediate consequence of the Adian-Rabin theorem, which shows that many natural properties of finitely presented groups are undecidable. In this paper, we prove an Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs, showing that many natural properties of the quantum automorphism group of a graph (including having quantum symmetries) are undecidable. We also show that it's undecidable to determine if the discrete quantum automorphism group is non-trivial. Our methods are based on solution groups of linear system nonlocal games, and we also prove an Adian-Rabin theorem in this context.

title: Dihedral pointed fusion categories: diagrammatics, 3-cocycle representatives, and planar algebras
summary: We construct a diagrammatic presentation by generators and relations for all dihedral pointed fusion categories $\mathrm{Vec}_{\mathrm{D}_{2n}}^ω$. Applying a jellyfish algorithm on our diagrammatics, we obtain an explicit closed formula for a complete set of normalized 3-cocycle representatives of $\mathrm{D}_{2n}$. As applications of our diagrammatics, we prove a universal property and show that in some cases we can recover affine $A$ unshaded subfactor planar algebras. We then extend our presentation to obtain diagrammatics for all pivotal structures on $\mathrm{Vec}_{\mathrm{D}_{2n}}^ω$.

title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
summary: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

title: On stable twist 2-groups of quasi-Hopf algebras
summary:
For any finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebra $A$, we define the notion of a stable twist of $A$. We show that stable twists form a strict 2-group $\2ust(A)$, which is equivalent to $\OAut(\C{A})^{\rev}$. Given a group homomorphism $ρ: G \to \ost(A)$, we determine the obstruction in $H^3(G,Z_G(A))$ to lift $ρ$ to a $G$-action on $\C{A}$. We also establish a bijection between such liftings and cocentral cleft extensions of $\k[G]$ by $A$.
  The main application of $\2ust(A)$ is the computation of $\OAut(\C{A})$, together with an explicit description of the corresponding tensor autoequivalences. We apply this framework to pointed Hopf algebras $A$ that arise as central extensions of Taft algebras by cyclic groups, and we explicitly determine all of their tensor autoequivalences. The equivariantizations of $\C{A}$ by $\ost(A)$ produce a new family of Hopf algebras $\N(n,ξ)$ of dimension $2nm$, where $ξ$ is a scalar of order $m\mid n$ such that neither $\N(n,ξ)$ nor its dual has the Chevalley property.
  In dimension 24, we prove that $\N(6,-1)$ and its dual are precisely the Hopf algebras $H$ for which neither $H$ nor $H^*$ has the Chevalley property. This completes the classification of nonsemisimple Hopf algebras of dimension 24.

title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
summary: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
summary: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
summary: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

title: Formality transmission
summary: Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences. These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc. In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission. This unifying framework allows us to extend these criteria in several directions, beyond characteristic zero and to differential graded algebras over operads or properads, leading to diverse new formality results.

title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
summary: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

title: Affinizations and braided module categories
summary: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object. We give explicit presentations of twisted affinizations, both as monoidal categories and as module categories, using invertible dots and reflection relations. We also describe the relation to cylinder twists and tensor-pair cylinder twists, including the naturality condition needed to obtain a braided module structure. As applications, we obtain module-category presentations of the affine Kauffman and affine oriented skein categories and an orientation-reversing twisted version of the latter. We realize the disoriented skein category as a quotient of this twisted affinization by a single additional relation.

title: Graded Automorphism of Multiparameter Quantum Matrix Algebra
summary: We determine the graded automorphism group of the multiparameter quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_{λ,\mathbf p}(M_n(\Bbbk))$ over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ for all $n\ge2$ and $λ\ne1$. No other restrictions are assumed on $\mathbf p$ or $λ$. Every graded automorphism is a torus automorphism, possibly followed by transposition or by simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices. We give the precise parameter conditions for these two involutions. As an application, we also determine the full automorphism group when the multiplicative group generated by the parameters is torsion-free.

title: Pre-modular fusion categories of global dimension $2p$
summary:
Let $p>5$ be a prime. In this paper, we show that a pre-modular fusion category of
  global dimension $2p$ is either pointed or tensor equivalent to $\text{Rep}(D_{2p})$.

title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
summary: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given.

title: Positivity of the Mirabolic Quantum Groups
summary: In this paper, we construct the canonical basis for the modified mirabolic quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. We then study the associated $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-module and $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-comodule structures and prove the positivity of this basis with respect to these two structures.

title: Graftings and cograftings for species
summary: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. We establish universal properties for the species of rooted forests. Using Fock functors, we recover the classical Connes--Kreimer Hopf algebra, its noncommutative planar analogue, and Foissy's $q$-infinitesimal Hopf algebra.

title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
summary: We prove a Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.

title: Tensor products of 2-representations
summary: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
summary:
In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials. As a result, we verify `in components' the Cayley-Hamilton and the reciprocal relations, obtained earlier with the use of the R-matrix techniques. We explicitly calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of quantum matrices and propose a
  conjecture regarding the form of the Hilbert-Poincaré series for the RTT-algebra.

title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
summary: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $Π_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[ρ]\in H^3(BG,Π_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=Π_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.

title: Reverse Module Categories of Vertex Operator Algebras
comment: 24 pages, correct some errors in Section 4
summary: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.

title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
comment: (v2) The proof is simplified and shortened further relative to the previous version. A discussion about the Lie brackets and the generators is added (v3) A proof of the closure of grt(F_2) under the Ihara bracket is added. (v4) Added Section 4.4 on the OpenAI injectivity argument
summary: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.

title: Webs and finite dimensional representation theory for quantum symmetric pairs
summary: We develop a highest weight framework and construct explicit finite dimensional irreducible modules for the type AIII (quasi split) quantum symmetric pair subalgebras $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$. In Part 1, we provide a uniform construction of Cartan subalgebras and Verma modules for both subfamilies. Our construction recovers Letzter's Cartan subalgebra in one subfamily and gives a new Cartan subalgebra in the other. We construct a weak triangular decomposition of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$ via the Letzter map. Then we define Verma modules as induced modules and prove that finite dimensional simple $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$-modules are quotients of our Verma modules. In Part 2, we define a diagrammatic category $Web^B$ that controls polynomial representations of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$. We prove a multiplicity-free decomposition of the quantum exterior powers $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$ as a $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$-module, using a explicit eigenspace decomposition of certain dot morphisms in $Web^B$. As applications, we deduce the multiplicity-freeness of the involved anti-spherical Hecke module. For $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$, we explicitly determine the highest weight vectors and their weights, thereby determining the isomorphism classes of their irreducible summands. Finally, we determine the kernel of the $Web^B$-action on certain finite dimensional representation category of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$.

title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
comment: 85 pages, comments welcome! Additions and changes in version 3: Broken links fixed
summary:
We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result.
  Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.

title: UCP Maps on Finite Toeplitz Systems
comment: Title updated following the removal of Gromov-Hausdorff convergence from the manuscript; accepted for publication in IMRN
summary: We study unital completely positive (UCP) maps on the finite Toeplitz operator system $\mathcal T_d$ of $d \times d$ Toeplitz matrices. We give an explicit characterization of pure UCP maps on $\mathcal T_d$ taking values in $M_n$ in terms of positive $n\times n$ matrix-valued trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $d-1$. This characterization yields a checkable criterion for deciding whether a given UCP map is pure. As an application, we prove that every pure UCP map on $\mathcal T_d$ has a unique completely positive extension to the generated $C^*$-algebra.

title: Maximality Levels of the classical permutation group in the quantum permutation group
comment: v2: Substantially revised and expanded. Maximality at moment level six established for all $N$ with assistance from ChatGPT. Includes a new computational appendix and publicly available Maple code
summary: Progress on the conjecture of Banica and Bichon that the classical permutation group is a maximal quantum subgroup of the quantum permutation group remains limited to a handful of small-parameter results. By Tannaka--Krein duality, any counterexample to this Maximality Conjecture must arise from a category strictly intermediate between the category $\mathcal{NC}$ of non-crossing partitions and the category $\mathcal{P}$ of all partitions. Any such exotic category must therefore contain a linear combination of crossing-partition vectors. The categories generated by $\mathcal{NC}$ together with some such vectors are studied, with a number of generation results. It is shown that no exotic category can contain a linear combination of three crossing-partition vectors, and, using an argument of ChatGPT to account for a five-dimensional gap, there is no exotic category distinguished from $\mathcal{NC}$ or $\mathcal{P}$ at moments of order six.

title: A Cohomology Theory of Supercommutative Algebras and Grading-Restricted Vertex Superalgebras
summary: This paper constructs the cohomology theory for grading-restricted vertex superalgebras, generalizing Yi-Zhi Huang's cohomology theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras. To simplify the discussion, motivate the construction, and make it easier for the reader to understand the technical points, we also include the construction of the cohomology theory of supercommutative associative algebras, a generalization of the Harrison cohomology theory of a commutative algebra that has not been explicitly written down. The paper will serve as the foundation for many subsequent studies, especially the deformation theory of vertex superalgebras.

title: Pointed Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10
comment: Corrected labels and added a previously omitted isomorphism class in dimension 8. Corrigendum submitted to the journal
summary: By utilizing the technique introduced in our previous work to construct Hopf superalgebras by reversing the Radford-Majid bosonization, we classify non-semisimple pointed Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

title: Frobenius kernels of algebraic supergroups and Steinberg's tensor product theorem
comment: This version corrects errors in the published article. An erratum has been submitted to Algebras and Representation Theory
summary: For a split quasireductive supergroup $G$ defined over a field, we study structure and representation of Frobenius kernels $G_r$ of $G$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $G_r$ to be unimodular in terms of the root system of $G$. We also establish Steinberg's tensor product theorem for $G$ under some natural assumptions.
